source_text: Cum esset Iesus in Hiericho, vidit virum gladium evaginatum tenentem: Noster es an adversariorum? Ego sum princeps militiae Domini. Adoravit Iesus — nolite omni spiritui credere; cognovit Deum. Quis princeps militiae nisi Dominus noster Iesus Christus, sub quo omnis militia caeli militat? Solve calceamentum — locus sanctus; Hiericho hostibus retenta sanctificatur adventu principis. Si Deus adsistit, solvamus a pedibus animae vinculum mortale.
pass_a_gloss: When was Jesus in Jericho, he-saw man sword unsheathed holding: Ours are-you or of-adversaries? I am prince of-army of-Lord. Worshiped Jesus — do-not to-every spirit believe; he-knew God. Who prince of-army unless Lord our Jesus Christ, under whom every army of-heaven serves? Loose sandal — place holy; Jericho by-enemies held is-sanctified by-arrival of-prince. If God stands-by, let-us-loose from feet of-soul bond mortal.
pass_b_english: [[While Jesus was by Jericho he saw a man with drawn sword: Are you for us or for our adversaries? I am prince of the Lord’s host >> Bible:Joshua 5:13-14]]. Jesus worshiped — [[test the spirits >> Bible:1 John 4:1]]; he knew this was God. Who is that prince but our Lord Jesus Christ, under whom every heavenly host serves? [[Loose your sandal — the place is holy >> Bible:Joshua 5:15]]. Jericho held by enemies becomes holy by the prince’s coming. If God stands with us, let us loose mortal bonds from the soul’s feet — [[feet Jesus washes >> Bible:John 13:8]].
